claims.text: TypeSafe AI opened early access to Jev, its SystemOne model, in the week before this post (September 2026).
GeoDeploy compares AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud regions that offer managed Kubernetes and picks the best region per geo.
TypeSafe's Jev provides AI primitives (confidence scoring, multiple choice, yes/no 'noul' questions) that let apps, agents, and workflows make decisions based on context.

Jev exposes three primitives: choice() returns the pick, a probability distribution across all options, and a confidence; score() rates against a rubric; noul() answers a yes/no question with a single probability.
GeoDeploy's score() rubrics use 10 levels.
Because Jev only selects from closed sets and never writes code or does arithmetic, a hallucinated region or made-up Pulumi argument cannot happen by construction.
For each geo, GeoDeploy sends Jev a shortlist of up to 40 priced candidates.
GeoDeploy asks Jev in a single call for one selection, five quality scores, two hard noul checks, and a fallback choice.
The TypeSafe SDK package is `@typesafe-ai/sdk` and exports choice, noul, and score.
The TypeSafe SDK provides a TypeSafeClient with a systemOne method taking state and questions and returning answers.
GeoDeploy fetches live prices from the AWS Price List API, the Azure Retail Prices API, and the Google Cloud Billing Catalog.
GeoDeploy supports DNS through Route 53, NS1, or Cloudflare, and EKS/AKS/GKE and ECR/ACR/Artifact Registry modules.
The Pulumi Automation API runs a preview then an update with one stack per region, and GeoDeploy won't run unless cloud credentials pass readiness checks.
Every GeoDeploy run writes plan.json and plan.md.
TypeSafe advises to 'describe situations, not degrees' when writing rubrics.
GeoDeploy's ranking uses weight profiles: latency-optimized (default), balanced, residency-first, and failure-domain.

Weight profile values: latency-optimized cost 0.13/coverage 0.48/maturity 0.17/sprawl 0.1/arch 0.12; balanced 0.25/0.25/0.2/0.12/0.18; residency-first 0.12/0.12/0.38/0.23/0.15; failure-domain 0.08/0.17/0.48/0.15/0.12.

GeoDeploy confidence thresholds: data residency 0.95 (hard reject); new cluster region 0.90 (top three flagged for human); existing stack region 0.75 (keep existing); ingress/autoscaling module 0.85 (registry default); node-pool sizing 0.60 (bin-packing result); global floor 0.50 (drop AI path).
Each AiPathAborted carries the full attempt (state, questions, answers) so rejected answers land in the audit trail.

On gate failure, API timeout/error, or unreachable upstream, GeoDeploy falls back to deterministic cross-provider price comparison while enforcing residency and constraint checks; `geodeploy explain` shows why each region won.

In self-driving mode (`geodeploy monitor`), GeoDeploy checks CPU utilization and asks Jev one joint question with options no-change, scale-up:<geo>, scale-down:<geo>, shift:<from>-><to>, plus a disruption-risk check; code computes node-count changes.

In self-driving mode, above 0.85 confidence the resize is applied automatically; between 0.70 and 0.85 it is suggested for human approval; below 0.70 GeoDeploy falls back to a deterministic per-region rule.
CPU utilization alone makes a poor autoscaling metric and is usually paired with other signals such as latency and error rates.
GeoDeploy is open source at github.com/pulumi/devx-geodeploy.
The Pulumi Automation API page exists at /automation/.
